summary_md: **AgentsWatch ([@AgentsWatch](https://x.com/AgentsWatch/status/2116090040845586583))** covers Fan et al.'s *MASCAL* ([arXiv 2610.39927](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39927)), training agents to attach calibrated confidence so downstream agents can adopt or verify; on MuSiQue handoffs with Qwen3-8B it scores 59.0 versus 47.5 for task-only RL, and random confidence hurts; a follow-up separates the two experiments.

referenced_urls.title: Learning Calibrated Confidence for Multi-Agent Collaboration

relevance: Calibrated confidence signals for multi-agent handoffs.

media.description: Diagram contrasting handoffs without confidence and MASCAL's calibrated confidence.
Table 4: accuracy and Brier scores under upstream confidence interventions.
media.ocr_text: Table 4 from Fan and colleagues' MASCAL paper: accuracy and Brier score under upstream confidence interventions on a trained MASCAL system. In math answer review, replacing calibrated confidence with random values drops accuracy from 78.69 to 73.07; hiding it lets the downstream agent fall back to content judgment. Credit: Fan et al., arXiv:2610.39927.
